newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan buys 150,000 T wheat at $164.94 per tonne.
newsitem.headline: Jordan buys 150,000 T wheat at $164.94 per tonne.

text.p: Jordan purchased Thursday 150,000 tonnes Argentinian, Australian and Canadian red hard winter wheat at $164.94 per tonne in three equal lots for delivery in November, December and January, according to traders.
They said Jordan bought the wheat from Geneva-based Romak which will be supplying Australian, Canadian and Argentinian origin wheat.
The shipment is to be delivered in three lots of 50,000 tonnes each in November, December and January.
The tender is key to deciding whether the government goes ahead soon with a reduction in bread prices prompted by recent cheaper wheat prices, officials said.

Officials had said before the snap tender was announced on Oct 10 that the government may lower bread prices in Jordan if the offer levels are attractive enough. It had decided on the unusually large snap tender to cash on softer grain prices.
The decision to almost double bread prices in August in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms led to the worst civil unrest since riots in 1989, which were also sparked by government price rises.
Since August, Jordan has bought 140,000 tonnes of wheat at prices ranging from $191 to $206 per tonne, a drop of nearly 25 percent from a high of $275 per tonne in May.
Bread is a staple for Jordan's 4.2 million people who have a per capita gross domestic product of about $1,500 a year.
